slides.title: 5 car myths you're probably still falling for

slides.myth: Your car needs several minutes to warm up.
slides.fact: Modern engines warm up fastest by driving gently. Idling for about 30 seconds is plenty, even in the cold.
slides.source: U.S. Department of Energy, Clean Cities

slides.myth: Idling uses less gas than turning the engine off.
slides.fact: Idle for more than 10 seconds and you burn more fuel than if you shut the engine off and restarted it.
slides.source: U.S. Department of Energy, Argonne National Laboratory

slides.myth: Premium gas gives a regular engine more power.
slides.fact: If your car is built for regular, premium gets you no consistent gain in power, mileage or emissions. Check your owner's manual.

slides.myth: You have to change your oil every 3,000 miles.
slides.fact: That interval fit older oils. Most owner's manuals now say 5,000 to 7,500 miles, and some say more. Follow your manual.

slides.myth: Fill your tires to the number on the tire.
slides.fact: The number on the sidewall is the tire's maximum pressure. Your car's recommended pressure is on the sticker in the driver's door jamb.
